column1: # Cover search providers - read by concat-audio and convert-audio when nothing
# local gave a book or a long track a cover.
# This is the shipped table. To change it, copy it anywhere, edit the copy and
# point the coverSearchTable setting at it.
# One TAB-separated row per search, five columns. Blank lines and # lines are
# ignored. The rows are tried top to bottom among those whose content matches,
# and the first image a row finds is the cover: put the searches you trust most
# first.
# The columns:
#   content   what the audio probably is: podcast, audiobook or other. A file
#             name ending in a [YouTube id] - yt-dlp's default - or starting
#             with a yyyymmdd date, or a length from 30 to 200 minutes, reads
#             as a podcast; anything longer as an audiobook; a shorter one
#             as other. convert-audio reads 30 to 200 minutes it encodes in
#             stereo as an audiobook too: most likely a full-cast drama.
#   provider  how the answer is read: audible, amazon, itunes, openlibrary or
#             youtube. A new site needs a reader in medialib/lib/onlinecover.py;
#             a new address for a known one only needs a row.
#   match     how sure the answer has to be:
#               id      none: the address names the very video the file came
#                       from, by the {youtube_id} in its name.
#               strict  the title, and nothing that contradicts it - an author
#                       or channel, a running time - and at least one of those
#                       agreeing when the title alone is short.
#               loose   the title alone: another edition, another language, or
#                       the printed book instead of the audiobook.
#               show    the podcast's own name, for the show's artwork rather
#                       than the episode's.
#   pace      seconds between two requests to this provider, at least.
#   address   the request. {title}, {creator}, {query} (both together) and
#             {youtube_id} are filled in, URL-encoded; a row that needs one the
#             file does not have is passed over. youtube's address is handed
#             to yt-dlp: a ytsearchN: search, or a watch address.
# podcast: the video the name's id points at, when it has one - only the
# thumbnail download failed; else the episode searched on YouTube, where it
# usually came from; then the show's artwork.
podcast
